rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should establish a baseline for RNA-only models. This tests the simplest RNA encoder (pca_n2000) with singleprofile settings, isolating the effect of RNA modality. It clarifies whether RNA data alone provides useful signals before exploring multimodal or more complex configurations.

The existing evidence shows that config_001 (RNA-only, singleprofile, PCA encoder) achieves 0.4849 validation accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile with avgpool aggregation (config_002), isolating the impact of profile setting and aggregation. It directly addresses whether multiprofile improves performance while keeping RNA encoder consistent, reducing uncertainty about key design choices.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile (config_002, 0.5906 accuracy) outperforms singleprofile (config_001, 0.4849). This experiment tests whether upgrading the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 (config_002) to scvi_n200 while maintaining multiprofile and avgpool aggregation isolates the impact of RNA encoder quality. It directly addresses whether better RNA representations (scvi_n200) improve performance, a critical design choice with sparse evidence yet high potential impact.

Existing evidence shows that RNA-only multiprofile models with scvi_n200 encoder and avgpool aggregation (config_005) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.650). This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation (while keeping RNA encoder and profile setting constant) could further improve performance. It isolates the effect of aggregation method, a key design choice, and builds on the strong evidence from config_005. This balances exploitation of the promising RNA encoder and exploration of aggregation techniques.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile settings with scvi_n200 RNA encoder and transformer aggregation (config_006, 0.6529 accuracy) outperform pca_n2000 with avgpool (config_002, 0.5907). This experiment tests whether using transformer aggregation with pca_n2000 (config_003) could bridge the performance gap, clarifying if aggregation method or RNA encoder choice is more impactful. It isolates the effect of aggregation while keeping RNA encoder and profile settings consistent with prior high-performing configurations.

Existing evidence shows that RNA-only models with scvi_n200 encoder and multiprofile setting (config_006) achieve the highest accuracy (0.653). This experiment tests adding image data (resnet50) to this strong baseline, isolating the effect of multimodal fusion. It balances exploitation (building on a proven RNA-only success) and exploration (testing if image data improves performance), while avoiding unnecessary complexity (no fusion method changes).

Existing evidence shows that scvi_n200 RNA encoder (config_005/006) and resnet50 image encoder (config_030) perform well. This experiment tests whether weighted fusion (vs concat in config_030) improves multimodal performance while keeping RNA/image encoders and aggregation method consistent. It isolates the effect of fusion strategy, which is critical for multimodal models, and builds on prior success with scvi_n200 and resnet50.

Existing evidence shows that weighted fusion (config_031) outperforms concat (config_030) in multimodal settings. This experiment tests whether using transformer aggregation (instead of avgpool) with weighted fusion further improves performance, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It builds on the strong foundation of config_031 while exploring a key design choice with minimal changes.

The existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (config_039) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder with scgpt (a more complex model) while keeping the image encoder, aggregation, and fusion methods the same would improve performance. This isolates the effect of the RNA encoder choice, a critical design decision, and leverages the strong evidence from config_039 to explore a promising direction efficiently.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_039) achieve the highest accuracy. This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder with imagenet_vit_l (while keeping RNA encoder, aggregation, and fusion methods similar) improves performance, isolating the impact of the image encoder choice. It balances exploitation of the current top-performing configuration with exploration of a critical design decision.
